subject.title: fix: beta releases require manual reruns after plugin publication

question: Should beta publication be considered complete when core is live but plugin npm and ClawHub convergence are still asynchronously repairing, and what operator guarantee must the continuation provide if that repair stalls?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes beta completion semantics rather than only fixing a mechanical retry; repository policy treats release, fallback, and operator-action changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Approve beta-live with repair guarantees
options.body: Allow detached ecosystem convergence for beta releases only after the continuation reliably adopts or cancels delayed child work, reconciles already-published ClawHub artifacts, and retains visible repair evidence.

options.title: Keep ecosystem convergence blocking
options.body: Require plugin npm and ClawHub completion in the parent publish workflow so a beta is not live until the whole ecosystem is converged.

options.title: Pause the release-policy change
options.body: Land only independent readiness or validation improvements and defer detached beta completion semantics to a narrower release-owner proposal.

recommendation.title: Approve beta-live with repair guarantees
recommendation.body: Allow detached ecosystem convergence for beta releases only after the continuation reliably adopts or cancels delayed child work, reconciles already-published ClawHub artifacts, and retains visible repair evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch history shows the strongest available connection to the current release-controller and continuation design.
